title: Aim at an action, an ability, or avoiding an outcome

variants.label: ために · intended action

segments.role: 覚えるために states memorizing as the purpose of the deliberate practice. In this ordinary purpose reading, the learner intends both actions. Elsewhere ために can express a cause, so this pattern does not create a universal rule about who must perform every action.

example.translation: I practice every day in order to memorize kanji.
example.note: The practice serves the intended action of memorizing.

variants.change: 覚えるために states memorizing as the purpose of the deliberate practice. In this ordinary purpose reading, the learner intends both actions. Elsewhere ために can express a cause, so this pattern does not create a universal rule about who must perform every action.

variants.label: ように · target ability

segments.role: 覚える changes to the potential form 覚えられる. ように frames that ability as the desired result of practice. The complete phrase changes: swapping the endings alone would hide the shift from doing an intended action to attaining an ability. Purpose constructions can overlap in other contexts.

example.translation: I practice every day so that I can memorize kanji.
example.note: The target is becoming able to remember the characters.

variants.change: 覚える changes to the potential form 覚えられる. ように frames that ability as the desired result of practice. The complete phrase changes: swapping the endings alone would hide the shift from doing an intended action to attaining an ability. Purpose constructions can overlap in other contexts.

variants.label: ように · prevention

segments.role: 忘れない names the unwanted event in the negative. ように makes its nonoccurrence the goal. This changes the stated aim from acquiring knowledge to keeping it. Negative-form purpose ように is useful for precautions; this sentence is not giving a reason that forgetting has already occurred.

example.translation: I practice every day so that I do not forget kanji.
example.note: The same daily practice now aims to prevent forgetting.

variants.change: 忘れない names the unwanted event in the negative. ように makes its nonoccurrence the goal. This changes the stated aim from acquiring knowledge to keeping it. Negative-form purpose ように is useful for precautions; this sentence is not giving a reason that forgetting has already occurred.

question: Which version explicitly makes the goal an ability to remember kanji?
answers: 漢字を覚えるために、毎日練習しています。
漢字を覚えられるように、毎日練習しています。
漢字を忘れないように、毎日練習しています。
feedback: 覚えられる is the potential form, and 覚えられるように makes that ability the target. 覚えるために names the intended action; 忘れないように instead states a preventive goal.
